errors.text: The proposed optimum of 950–980 °C contradicts the target result that 1000 °C gives the best density, hardness, oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance.
The hypothesis incorrectly treats the 1000 °C sample as Mg-loss-damaged and porous, whereas the target reports 96.7% relative density and 1235.5 HV at 1000 °C.
The proposed Mg2Ti/Al2Ti Laves phases and TiO 'intermetallics' do not match the observed barrier phases AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3; TiO is an oxide, not an intermetallic.
Cr2O3-rich passivation and Ti/Cr/Mg film analysis are chemically inapplicable because the Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co alloy contains no chromium.
The predicted density above 98%, hardness merely above 650 HV, and corrosion current below 0.5 µA/cm² disagree with the reported 96.7%, 1235.5 HV, and 1.07 µA/cm².

The oxidation experiment is specified at 800 °C rather than the target condition of 900 °C and lacks a decisive model-selection rule comparing parabolic diffusion control against linear or surface-reaction-limited kinetics.
